title: Best New Sportsbooks (2026)
verdict: The best new sportsbooks of 2026 are not sportsbooks. They are the federally regulated sports exchanges and prediction markets that launched or relaunched nationwide this year: ProphetX (June), Novig (August) and Polymarket US (January), joining Kalshi. They price with no vig, never limit winners, and let you sell a position before the game ends. The best way to use all of them, with the sportsbooks you already have, is TerminalUp, which shows the best fee-adjusted price across the venues it connects to and routes the order there from one account.
Traditional sportsbook launches in 2026 were mostly existing brands entering additional states. Nothing new there changes the price. The venues below do.

faq.a: The notable launches were federally regulated exchanges and prediction markets: Polymarket US in January, ProphetX in June and Novig in August, all under CFTC designation. Traditional brands mostly expanded into additional states.

faq.q: Are the new prediction markets legal?
faq.a: They operate nationwide under CFTC designation. Sports contracts are contested by several states, with court orders restricting them in a few as of November 2026; each venue lists where it is live.
No. It is a peer-to-peer exchange: bettors trade against each other at prices with no vig, and Novig earns a fee. Since August 2026 it operates nationwide as a CFTC-designated market.

faq.q: Do new sportsbooks have better odds?
faq.a: New retail brands rarely do; they copy the market and add margin. The new exchanges and prediction markets do, because there is no margin in the price.

faq.q: Do new venues offer sign-up bonuses?
faq.a: The exchanges and prediction markets generally do not, because they take no margin to fund one. Their offer is the price.
Kalshi and Polymarket US on major games and futures; Novig and ProphetX on game lines as sports-only markets. Depth varies by game and hour, which is the case for a cross-venue board.
